# Mermaid v13 config reference

<!-- Generated by tools/gen-config from packages/core/schema/config.schema.yaml. Do not edit: run `pnpm gen:config`. -->

Every config key Mermaid accepts, with its v13 status:

- **honoured**: v13 implements it.
- **pending**: accepted without a warning; it takes effect once its diagram type or feature is ported (R-CONF-5).
- **ignored**: accepted without a warning, but has no effect in v13.
- **removed**: produces a warning and has no effect.
- **moved**: produces a warning; the key now belongs to another package.

Keys not listed here produce an "unknown key" warning and are dropped from diagram text. Diagram text (front matter and `%%{init}%%` directives) can never set the keys listed in `secure`, nor the integrator-only options `securityLevel`, limits, `deterministic`, `idPrefix`, `output.cssVariables`, the measurer, link schemes, `discovery` or `cdnBase`.

"padding" is `flowchart.padding`. Plain `redux` and `redux-dark` carry no per-subgraph palette; every theme carries v12's `cScale`, `cScaleInv` and `cScaleLabel` (D258). `neo` carries the redux values of the geometry, ER and `classText` variables (v12 `look: neo`, D181) and no per-subgraph palette, with its own corner (`radius` 3) and shadow (`drop-shadow(0 1px 2px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.25))`); `neo-dark` the same, with `drop-shadow(1px 2px 2px rgb(185 185 185 / 0.2))`. Geometry variables are read as numbers at render time, because they feed layout, so overriding their CSS variables has no effect; `dropShadow` is a CSS value. |  |

| `architecture.useMaxWidth` | boolean | `true` | pending |  | When this flag is set to `true`, the height and width is set to 100% and is then scaled with the available space. If set to `false`, the absolute space required is used. |
| `architecture.theme` | "default" \\| "base" \\| "dark" \\| "forest" \\| "neutral" \\| "neo" \\| "neo-dark" \\| "redux" \\| "redux-dark" \\| "redux-color" \\| "redux-dark-color" \\| "null" |  | pending |  | Theme, the CSS style sheet. You may also use `themeCSS` to override this value. |
| `architecture.look` | "classic" \\| "handDrawn" \\| "neo" |  | ignored (13.0.0) | `look` is removed (D153): ignored, with one `LOOK_REMOVED` warning per render, whatever the diagram section. Replacement: `theme`, or the geometry and `dropShadow` theme variables. | Defines which main look to use for the diagram. |
| `architecture.layout` | string |  | pending |  | Defines which layout algorithm to use for rendering the diagram. |
| `architecture.padding` | number | `40` | pending |  |  |
| `architecture.iconSize` | number | `80` | pending |  |  |
| `architecture.fontSize` | number | `16` | pending |  |  |
| `architecture.randomize` | boolean | `false` | pending |  | Whether to randomize initial node positions before running the layout algorithm. When false (default), nodes start at deterministic seed positions. When true, nodes start at random positions, which may produce varied but potentially better-spaced layouts. Note: `randomize: false` alone does NOT guarantee identical renders, because the underlying fcose layout still uses `Math.random()` internally during its constraint solver — use the `seed` option for full determinism. |
| `architecture.nodeSeparation` | number | `75` | pending |  | Minimum separation (in pixels) between sibling nodes in the same group, passed through to the underlying fcose layout. Increase to spread overlapping siblings apart when many edges share the same port direction. |
| `architecture.idealEdgeLengthMultiplier` | number | `1.5` | pending |  | Multiplier applied to `iconSize` to compute the ideal length of edges between nodes within the same group. Increase to add breathing room; decrease to pack the diagram tighter. Edges crossing group boundaries are unaffected and use a fixed shorter length. |
| `architecture.edgeElasticity` | number | `0.45` | pending |  | Spring elasticity (0–1) applied to edges between nodes within the same group, passed through to fcose. Higher values pull connected nodes closer together; lower values let the layout spread them out. Edges crossing group boundaries are unaffected. |
| `architecture.numIter` | number | `2500` | pending |  | Maximum number of iterations the fcose layout algorithm runs before stopping. Increase for higher quality on large or densely-connected diagrams at the cost of render time. |
| `architecture.seed` | number | `1` | pending |  | Deterministic seed for the fcose layout. Defaults to 1, which makes every render of the same diagram produce the same layout — required for visual regression tests to be stable. Set to 0 to opt out and use the unstubbed Math.random (the layout will still differ slightly between renders, matching pre-fix behavior). Any other number selects a different reproducible layout variant. |

## `c4`

| Key | Type | Default | Status | Notes | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `c4` | object |  | honoured (13.0.0) |  | The object containing configurations specific for c4 diagrams |
| `c4.useWidth` | number |  | ignored (13.0.0) | Only v12's gantt renderer read `useWidth`; the C4 renderer never did. |  |
| `c4.useMaxWidth` | boolean | `true` | honoured (13.0.0) | As v12: true draws `width="100%"` and a `max-width`; false draws the diagram at its own `width` and `height`. | When this flag is set to `true`, the height and width is set to 100% and is then scaled with the available space. If set to `false`, the absolute space required is used. |
| `c4.theme` | "default" \\| "base" \\| "dark" \\| "forest" \\| "neutral" \\| "neo" \\| "neo-dark" \\| "redux" \\| "redux-dark" \\| "redux-color" \\| "redux-dark-color" \\| "null" |  | honoured (13.0.0) | Set here, it wins over the top-level `theme` for C4 diagrams (a diagram section beats the top level within a config layer). | Theme, the CSS style sheet. You may also use `themeCSS` to override this value. |
| `c4.look` | "classic" \\| "handDrawn" \\| "neo" |  | ignored (13.0.0) | `look` is removed (D153): ignored, with one `LOOK_REMOVED` warning per render, whatever the diagram section. Replacement: `theme`, or the geometry and `dropShadow` theme variables. | Defines which main look to use for the diagram. |
| `c4.layout` | string |  | ignored (13.0.0) | C4 lays out with its own grid and relation router (`layoutKind: 'custom'`, D454, D455), as v12 had its own packer; neither the top-level nor a C4-scoped `layout` changes it. | Defines which layout algorithm to use for rendering the diagram. |
| `c4.diagramMarginX` | integer | `50` | honoured (13.0.0) | The canvas margin left and right of what is drawn, and the gap between boundaries side by side (D454). | Margin to the right and left of the c4 diagram, must be a positive value. |
| `c4.diagramMarginY` | integer | `10` | honoured (13.0.0) | The canvas margin above and below what is drawn, and with `c4ShapeMargin` the gap between boundaries one under the other (D454). The title row (60 px) is above it. | Margin to the over and under the c4 diagram, must be a positive value. |
| `c4.c4ShapeMargin` | integer | `50` | honoured (13.0.0) | Elements sit `2 · c4ShapeMargin` apart both ways, as v12's packer; a boundary's contents sit `c4ShapeMargin` inside its frame on every side, below its header (D454). | Margin between shapes |
| `c4.c4ShapePadding` | integer | `20` | honoured (13.0.0) | The room round an element's text: an element is at least its text's width plus `2 · c4ShapePadding`, as v12's classic look; it also sizes the cylinder, queue and `fr-rect` padding in the classic themes. | Padding between shapes |
| `c4.width` | integer | `216` | honoured (13.0.0) | The least width of an element, as v12; a boundary's header wraps at its contents' width or this, whichever is wider. A number of 0 or more (or a numeric string); anything else lays out with the default. | Width of person boxes |
| `c4.height` | integer | `60` | ignored (13.0.0) | v12's C4 renderer never read it: an element is as tall as its text (D454). | Height of person boxes |
| `c4.boxMargin` | integer | `10` | ignored (13.0.0) | v12's C4 renderer never read it (D454). | Margin around boxes |
| `c4.c4ShapeInRow` | integer | `4` | honoured (13.0.0) | The elements in a row: a default that `UpdateLayoutConfig`'s `$c4ShapeInRow` overrides; v12 hard-coded 4 and never read the key (D454). An integer of 1 or more; anything else lays out with the default. | How many shapes to place in each row. |
| `c4.nextLinePaddingX` | number | `0` | honoured (13.0.0) | Each row of elements after the first starts this far in, as v12's packer. |  |
| `c4.c4BoundaryInRow` | integer | `2` | honoured (13.0.0) | The boundaries in a row: a default that `UpdateLayoutConfig`'s `$c4BoundaryInRow` overrides; v12 hard-coded 2 and never read the key (D454). ## `sankey`

| Key | Type | Default | Status | Notes | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sankey` | object |  | honoured (13.0.0) |  | The object containing configurations specific for sankey diagrams. |
| `sankey.useWidth` | number |  | ignored (13.0.0) | Only v12's gantt renderer read `useWidth`; the sankey renderer never did. |  |
| `sankey.useMaxWidth` | boolean | `true` | honoured (13.0.0) | v12 documented `false`, but its bundled defaults held `true` and every sankey without the key drew `width="100%"` with a `max-width`; v13 keeps that output. False draws the diagram's own `width` and `height`; a value that is not a boolean is the default and warns `SANKEY_CONFIG_INVALID`. |  |
| `sankey.theme` | "default" \\| "base" \\| "dark" \\| "forest" \\| "neutral" \\| "neo" \\| "neo-dark" \\| "redux" \\| "redux-dark" \\| "redux-color" \\| "redux-dark-color" \\| "null" |  | pending |  | Theme, the CSS style sheet. You may also use `themeCSS` to override this value. |
| `sankey.look` | "classic" \\| "handDrawn" \\| "neo" |  | ignored (13.0.0) | `look` is removed (D153): ignored, with one `LOOK_REMOVED` warning per render, whatever the diagram section. Replacement: `theme`, or the geometry and `dropShadow` theme variables. | Defines which main look to use for the diagram. |
| `sankey.layout` | string |  | pending |  | Defines which layout algorithm to use for rendering the diagram. |
| `sankey.width` | number | `600` | honoured (13.0.0) | A number of 0 or more, or a numeric string as its number; anything else (negative, not a number) lays out with the default and warns `SANKEY_CONFIG_INVALID`, where v12 passed it to d3-sankey as it was. |  |
| `sankey.height` | number | `400` | honoured (13.0.0) | A number of 0 or more, or a numeric string as its number; anything else (negative, not a number) lays out with the default and warns `SANKEY_CONFIG_INVALID`, where v12 passed it to d3-sankey as it was. |  |
| `sankey.linkColor` | any | `"gradient"` | honoured (13.0.0) | `gradient`, `source`, `target` or one CSS colour for every link. A colour that fails the colour check draws the default `gradient` and warns `SANKEY_COLOR_INVALID`. | The color of the links in the sankey diagram. |
| `sankey.nodeAlignment` | object | `"justify"` | honoured (13.0.0) | An unknown value lays out with the default and warns `SANKEY_CONFIG_INVALID`. | Controls the alignment of the Sankey diagrams. See <https://github.com/d3/d3-sankey#alignments>. |

Constrained the same way as `actorFontWeight`. |
| `usecase.nodeSpacing` | number | `50` | honoured (13.0.0) | A number, or a numeric string, from the minimum below 10000; anything else draws with the default and adds one `USECASE_CONFIG_IGNORED` warning. | Spacing between nodes on the same level |
| `usecase.rankSpacing` | number | `50` | honoured (13.0.0) | A number, or a numeric string, from the minimum below 10000; anything else draws with the default and adds one `USECASE_CONFIG_IGNORED` warning. | Spacing between nodes on different levels |
| `usecase.diagramPadding` | number | `20` | honoured (13.0.0) | A number, or a numeric string, from the minimum below 10000; anything else draws with the default and adds one `USECASE_CONFIG_IGNORED` warning. | Padding around the entire diagram |
| `usecase.colorScheme` | "role" \\| "rotate" | `"role"` | honoured (13.0.0) | As in v12, also when an author's `borderColorArray` gives a theme without one a palette (D474). Any other value colours by role and adds one `USECASE_CONFIG_IGNORED` warning. | How a use case diagram takes its colours from the active theme. `role` (the default) gives every element of a kind one colour, read from the `usecaseActorBkg` / `usecaseActorBorder`, `usecaseBkg` / `usecaseBorder`, and `usecaseBoundaryBkg` / `usecaseBoundaryBorder` theme variables. Colour then says what an element *is*, and it is invariant under insertion, reordering, and renaming -- adding one use case in the middle does not recolour the ones after it, so diffs, documentation screenshots, and visual baselines stay stable. `rotate` instead gives each actor, use case, and system boundary its own slot from the theme's categorical palette (`borderColorArray` / `bkgColorArray`), the way ER entities and class boxes are coloured. Actors and use cases share one cycle, and system boundaries run a second one from zero, so a boundary is never forced to match an element inside it. Within the shared cycle the actors are numbered first and the use cases after them, each in declaration order -- an interleaved `actor A`, `usecase U`, `actor B` is therefore numbered A, B, U rather than A, U, B. This buys per-instance variety at the cost of the stability `role` has: inserting an element shifts the colour of every later element of its own kind, and inserting an actor shifts the use cases too. Only the colour themes (`redux-color`, `redux-dark-color`) carry a palette, so on every other theme the two settings render identically. `classDef` and `style` keep overriding both, whichever is set. |

| `cynefin.seed` | number | `0` | honoured (13.0.0) | v12 hashed the SVG element id, which changed with every render id; v13 hashes the render's `idPrefix` with v12's hash (D362). When 0 (the default) the seed is a hash of the render's id prefix (the `id` render option, or one derived from the text and config), so a render is deterministic for a given id and two diagrams on one page differ. ## `elk` (plugin `@mermaid-js/layout-elk`)

Known only while `@mermaid-js/layout-elk` is registered.

| Key | Type | Default | Status | Notes | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `elk` | object |  | honoured |  | Options of the ELK layouts (`layout: elk`, `elk.<algorithm>` and the `flowchart-elk` header), with v12 develop's defaults (D174). |
| `elk.mergeEdges` | boolean | `false` | honoured |  | Elk specific option that allows edges to share path where it convenient. It can make for pretty diagrams but can also make it harder to read the diagram. |
| `elk.nodePlacementStrategy` | "SIMPLE" \\| "NETWORK_SIMPLEX" \\| "LINEAR_SEGMENTS" \\| "BRANDES_KOEPF" |  | honoured |  | Elk specific option affecting how nodes are placed. |
| `elk.nodePlacementAlignment` | "NONE" \\| "LEFTUP" \\| "LEFTDOWN" \\| "RIGHTUP" \\| "RIGHTDOWN" \\| "BALANCED" |  | honoured |  | Elk specific option affecting Brandes-Koepf node placement alignment. BALANCED combines the four directional alignments; NONE picks the smallest result. Defaults to BALANCED for the default preset and NONE for named non-default presets. |
| `elk.preset` | "default" \\| "legacy" \\| "modelOrder" \\| "depthFirst" | `"default"` | honoured |  | Named combination of layering, node placement, placement alignment and cycle breaking options. Explicit options override the preset for that option; the remaining preset values still apply. `default` — network simplex layering, balanced Brandes-Koepf placement at the top level and inside subgraphs, and depth-first cycle breaking. Balanced placement favors centered branches and composite-state entries, sometimes at the cost of a wider or taller drawing. It does not guarantee that every edge attaches to the center of its target. `legacy` — Brandes-Koepf placement with NONE alignment and ELK's own greedy cycle breaking. Reproduces the rendering before presets existed. `modelOrder` — network simplex layering and top-level placement, Brandes-Koepf placement inside subgraphs, NONE alignment, and greedy model-order cycle breaking, which favors declaration order. `depthFirst` — the previous default: network simplex layering and top-level placement, Brandes-Koepf placement inside subgraphs, NONE alignment, and depth-first cycle breaking. Setting `layeringStrategy`, `nodePlacementStrategy`, `nodePlacementAlignment` or `cycleBreakingStrategy` explicitly overrides the preset for that option, including an explicit NONE alignment. |
| `elk.straightenEdges` | boolean | `true` | honoured |  | Straightens an edge that leaves or enters a node with a tiny step. ELK spreads an edge's port evenly along a node's side but routes the edge down a channel whose row rarely lines up with that port exactly, leaving a staircase of a few pixels right at the border. With rounded corners the two micro-bends land on top of each other and read as a kink. Enabling this moves the channel onto the port's row and drops the step, so the edge draws as one straight line and both ports stay exactly where the layout put them. Only the step next to a node is touched, and only when the edge continues the same way afterwards, so a real turn is never collapsed. An edge is left alone entirely when moving its run would drag the far port, or would introduce a crossing. |
| `elk.lineHops` | any | `true` | honoured |  | Renders edge crossings as small arcs ("hops") or visible gaps, so that it is clear which line passes over which where two edges meet. Of a horizontal and a vertical run, the horizontal one gives way; otherwise the later edge does. Only straight runs carry hops: curves and rounded corners are left as drawn, and a crossing too close to a bend gets no hop. `true` and `arc` draw an arc, `gap` breaks the line. Set to `false` to draw plain crossings. |
| `elk.layeringStrategy` | "NETWORK_SIMPLEX" \\| "LONGEST_PATH" \\| "LONGEST_PATH_SOURCE" \\| "COFFMAN_GRAHAM" \\| "MIN_WIDTH" \\| "STRETCH_WIDTH" \\| "INTERACTIVE" |  | honoured |  | Elk specific option deciding which layer each node is assigned to — the column in a left-to-right diagram, the row in a top-down one. This is the coarsest of the three placement decisions, so changing it moves nodes further than anything else short of altering spacing. NETWORK_SIMPLEX aims for the fewest long edges. LONGEST_PATH pushes every node as late as it can go. COFFMAN_GRAHAM bounds how many nodes share a layer, giving a more even, block-like shape on wide graphs. MIN_WIDTH and STRETCH_WIDTH trade edge length for a narrower or wider drawing. INTERACTIVE honours positions already on the nodes. |
| `elk.layeringLayerBound` | number | `4` | honoured |  | Elk specific option capping how many nodes COFFMAN_GRAHAM will put in one layer. Ignored by every other layering strategy. Lower values give a taller, narrower drawing. |
| `elk.cycleBreakingStrategy` | "GREEDY" \\| "DEPTH_FIRST" \\| "INTERACTIVE" \\| "MODEL_ORDER" \\| "GREEDY_MODEL_ORDER" |  | honoured |  | This strategy decides how to find cycles in the graph and deciding which edges need adjustment to break loops. |
| `elk.forceNodeModelOrder` | boolean | `false` | honoured |  | The node order given by the model does not change to produce a better layout. E.g. if node A is before node B in the model this is not changed during crossing minimization. This assumes that the node model order is already respected before crossing minimization. This can be achieved by setting considerModelOrder.strategy to NODES_AND_EDGES. |
| `elk.considerModelOrder` | "NONE" \\| "NODES_AND_EDGES" \\| "PREFER_EDGES" \\| "PREFER_NODES" | `"NODES_AND_EDGES"` | honoured |  | Preserves the order of nodes and edges in the model file if this does not lead to additional edge crossings. Depending on the strategy this is not always possible since the node and edge order might be conflicting. |
| `elk.keepEntryNodeOnTop` | boolean | `false` | honoured |  | Elk specific option that keeps the entry node of a recursive flow at the top of the layout. When a flow loops back on itself (a back-edge to an earlier node), ELK's degree-based cycle-breaking has no notion of an "entry point" and may rank the first-declared node in the middle, scrambling the reading order. When enabled, the entry node of each cyclic component is pinned to the first layer so the diagram still reads from its entry. Acyclic flows always have a natural source, so this has no effect on them. Only applies when the cyclic flow has no node without incoming edges: if the loop is fed from outside (e.g. a start node pointing into it), that component already has a natural source and nothing is pinned. Detection is also scoped per container, so cycles that cross a subgraph boundary are not detected. |
| `elk.orientFeedbackEdges` | boolean | `true` | honoured |  | Routes an edge that re-enters a subgraph downstream instead of around the subgraph. ELK lays out a subgraph as one node of its parent graph. A node outside a subgraph that both receives an edge from it and sends one back into it therefore closes a cycle there, even when the nodes inside do not. ELK breaks that cycle by reversing one of the edges and routes it into the subgraph's input side, around the outside of the subgraph. When enabled, such edges are found before layout, on the graph with each subgraph collapsed, and handed to ELK in the other direction. The edge is drawn with its arrowhead at its real target. Cycles between plain nodes are left to `cycleBreakingStrategy`. |

## `handDrawnSeed` (plugin `@mermaid-js/plugin-hand-drawn`)

Known only while `@mermaid-js/plugin-hand-drawn` is registered.

| Key | Type | Default | Status | Notes | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `handDrawnSeed` | number | `0` | honoured (13.0.0) | 0 is a fixed seed, not a random one (D300). | The seed of the hand-drawn sketch. Every outline uses it, so the same text gives the same drawing on every render and machine, and another seed gives another drawing. A non-zero seed draws as v12 did for the same geometry. 0, the default, is a fixed seed too: v12 used a random one. |
